{'translation': 'The Labour Department announced today (the 10th) that Wah So Ice House Cafe (Prince Edward) is suspected of providing false information when applying to import foreign workers, and has been subjected to administrative sanctions by the department. The Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme has been in place for three years since its launch in September 2023. The Labour Department replied that as of July this year, a total of 1,365 complaints had been received, of which 111 warning letters were issued to employers suspected of violations, and another 17 cases involving illegal importation of foreign workers and 31 cases involving violations of other legislation resulting in convictions were subject to administrative sanctions. Together with Wah So Ice House Cafe (Prince Edward), whose sanctions were just announced today, Database Integrated News consolidated 18 companies punished for violating the rules on importing foreign workers, of which 10 are in the catering services and cleaning industries. Why were they punished? Among the 18 companies, 9 were involved in unreasonably refusing to hire local job seekers, and most were refused applications to import foreign workers for the following two years by the Labour Department; another two restaurants dismissed local employees after importing foreign workers, and their approved foreign worker quotas were revoked immediately.'}

{'translation': 'As of today, the Labour Department has imposed administrative sanctions on a total of 18 employers for violating the Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme, all of which have been suspended from processing applications for one to two years.'}

{'translation': "The Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme was launched in September 2023, but against the backdrop of a sluggish economy, rising unemployment and underemployment rates, the government's continued importation of foreign workers has drawn attention. In August 2025, the authorities announced the first administrative sanction case, involving a company refusing local job seekers without reasonable grounds, with the company's application terminated immediately and its foreign worker application for the following year refused. In late August of the same month, Secretary for Labour and Welfare Sun Yuk-han said the foreign worker mechanism must not be abused, and that in future, depending on the severity of cases and societal concerns, the names of violating employers would be disclosed where feasible."}

{'translation': 'Database Integrated News compiled administrative sanction cases previously made public by the Labour Department. Together with Wah So Ice House Cafe (Prince Edward), which was sanctioned today, the Labour Department has imposed administrative sanctions on at least 18 employers for violating the rules on importing foreign workers, of which 6 are in the catering services industry and 4 are cleaning services companies. Nine companies were sanctioned for refusing to hire local job seekers without reasonable grounds, including Toto Toto (Tsuen Wan) Limited, Asia Cleaning Services, and Sin Hang Procare Elderly Home, among others; the positions involved include general clerks, warehouse keepers, cleaners, air-conditioning technical assistants, and more. Among the nine companies, eight were refused foreign worker applications for the following two years by the Labour Department.'}

{'translation': 'Last August, Sheung Yuan was administratively sanctioned by the Labour Department for dismissing local employees after hiring foreign workers. (File photo)'}

{'translation': 'In addition, five companies are suspected of providing false information, submitting untrue applicant information, local employee numbers, and public recruitment results to the Labour Department, including Little Girl Exchange Limited, Tai Lie Frozen Meat, Wah So Ice House Cafe (Prince Edward), among others, all of which had their applications suspended for one year.'}

{'translation': 'In two cases, Sheung Yuan Banquet Hall Limited, which operates Sheung Yuan Chinese Cuisine Restaurant, and Zhan Neng Group Limited, which operates Ying Yuen, were found to have dismissed local workers after hiring foreign workers. Both were refused applications for the following two years and had their approved importation of worker approvals revoked immediately. However, for the 11 foreign worker quotas already used by Sheung Yuan Chinese Cuisine Restaurant, foreign workers already employed may continue to remain in Hong Kong for work; Secretary for Labour and Welfare Sun Yuk-han said at the time that the punishment provided sufficient deterrent effect on employers.'}

{'translation': 'Three years into the implementation of the Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme, the Labour Department received a total of 1,365 complaints, of which approximately 8% of cases were issued warning letters and approximately 3% were subjected to administrative sanctions. (File photo)'}

{'translation': 'Complaints increased tenfold last year year-on-year; 533 complaints received in the first seven months of this year'}

{'translation': "The Labour Department replied to Database Integrated News' enquiry that as of July this year, the Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme had received a total of 1,365 complaints, of which 14 were in 2023, 69 in 2024, and 749 in 2025, representing a year-on-year increase of nearly tenfold. As for the first seven months of this year, 533 complaints had already been received. Of the 1,365 complaints, for cases where investigations had been completed, the Labour Department issued 111 warning letters to employers suspected of violations, accounting for approximately 8% of complaints; meanwhile, 17 cases involved violations of the Scheme's regulations and were subjected to administrative sanctions, suspended from processing foreign worker importation applications for one to two years. Additionally, 31 employers were subjected to administrative sanctions for illegal activity resulting in convictions, including the Employees' Compensation Ordinance, occupational safety and health legislation, and the Immigration Ordinance."}

{'translation': 'In response to labour sector concerns over local worker unemployment, the authorities completed a review of the Scheme in mid-June this year, introducing a two-tier approval system in the catering services industry, tightening the ratio of local full-time employees to foreign workers from 2:1 to 3:1, and extending the maximum administrative sanction period for violating employers to five years. In June and July after the introduction of the two-tier system, the Scheme received 94 and 85 complaints respectively, with the catering industry remaining the hardest hit, accounting for 49 and 53 complaints respectively over the past two months, representing nearly 57%.'}
